chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj al-Ifrad. He arrived in Mecca, circumambulated the House, prayed two cycles near the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and performed Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him exit Ihram and make it a Tamattu' Hajj, unless he had brought the sacrificial animal (Hady).'

key_terms.سَعَى: Performed Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.لَبَّى: Exclaimed the Talbiyya, entering the state of Ihram for Hajj
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.مُفْرِدًا: Performing Hajj al-Ifrad (single Hajj without Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who performs all rituals of Hajj al-Ifrad but wants to convert it to Tamattu?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the flexibility of Hajj al-Ifrad, ruling that completing all pillars without an intermediate Ihram exit does not invalidate the act but rather allows the pilgrim to convert it into Hajj al-Tamattu' by performing Qurb al-Tawaf and Sa'i. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the distinction between Ifrad and Tamattu' often lies in the intention and the handling of the Hady (sacrificial animal) rather than rigid procedural separation. The exception for those who brought the Hady underscores the importance of fulfilling specific obligations tied to the chosen form of pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who exclaimed Talbiyya with the exclusive Hajj. He proceeded to Makkah and circumambulated with the House (Kabah), and Prayed two Cycles by the Standing Place of Ibrahimas, and performed Sa’ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa’. Heasws said: ‘So let him be free (from Ihraam), and let him make it to be a Tamatto, unless if he happens to be ushering the sacrificial animal’.
